isolation: Each scenario signed in as its own test account (test-employee=Ruwan, test-employee-2=Nadeeka, test-manager=Malith, test-manager-2=Sanduni, test-finance-admin=Dilani) and created the claims/policy rules it asserts on through the real UI or a direct API call as its own Given. The meals policy-rule cap has no version history, so each scenario needing a specific cap value (20,000 or 25,000) set it explicitly via API/UI immediately before acting, rather than assuming a prior value. Meals-cap monthly totals cannot be reset (no delete-claim endpoint), so 'has not claimed any meals this month' scenarios used Nadeeka (verified via GET /me/claims to hold zero meals claims all month) while 'has already claimed' scenarios used Ruwan, seeded with one real 15,000 LKR meals claim before the flagging scenarios ran.

steps.text: Ruwan the employee has uploaded a photo of a receipt from "Spice Garden Restaurant" dated "2026-09-12" for "8500" LKR
steps.observed: A synthetic receipt image (rendered from HTML: merchant 'Spice Garden Restaurant', date 2026-09-12, total 8,500 LKR) was selected into the New Claim screen's file input.

steps.text: the receipt is read
steps.observed: The upload triggers a POST to /api/receipt-agent/chat (the webapp's own same-origin proxy), which answered 401. The whole app navigated to /forbidden.

steps.text: the claim form shows merchant "Spice Garden Restaurant", date "2026-09-12", total "8500" and a category
steps.observed: Timed out — the New Claim form was never shown again; the page is on /forbidden ('Not available to you — That screen needs a permission your account does not have.'). No fields were ever filled. Reproduced twice, identically. Root cause isolated: the SAME token, called directly against the receipt-agent service (POST {receipt-agent-url}/chat) instead of through the webapp's proxy, returns 200 and a correct reply — proving the token/scope are valid and the defect is in the webapp's own reverse-proxy-to-gateway wiring for /api/receipt-agent/*, not a permissions gap.
